$comment: /build-cycles/ — Build, the owner page for Build Cycles: what a cycle is, how it runs (the home page's Build scenes, in one place), the current cycle's state (from content/cycles, decided by the clock), what it isn't, and the one action, the account. Each cycle also has its own page (/build-cycles/<id>/).

meta.need: As someone thinking about a Build Cycle, I need to know what it is, what it asks, when the next one starts and how to apply, so that I can decide to go for it.

title: Build Cycles
description: A Build Cycle is twelve weeks where strangers pick a problem worth solving, team up, and make something that helps. Free, in person at your local public library, by application.

hero.title: Make something real.
hero.lede: A Build Cycle is twelve weeks where strangers pick a problem worth solving, team up, and make something that helps.

state.$comment: The current cycle's band, by its state (src/lib/dates.ts). {title}, {kickoff} and {showcase} are filled from the cycle.

open.title: {title} starts {kickoff}.
open.body: It's free, and places are limited. Make your free account, then apply from there.

underway.title: The next cycle is coming.
underway.body: Applications have closed, and the teams are building. You don't have to wait to get involved.
underway.cta: Hear when the next cycle opens

done.title: The next cycle is coming.
done.body: The last one ended at its Showcase. Join, and your account tells you when the next one opens.
done.cta: Hear when the next cycle opens

how.title: Strangers become a Pod. Then a team.

steps.title: Kickoff
steps.body: It starts in one room, at the Summit, with the problem situations: real, messy problems people face.

steps.title: A Pod
steps.body: Everyone joins a group of nine or more, called a Pod, around a problem situation you choose together. It can feel uncertain at first. That's normal: everyone finds a Pod, and a Poderator keeps it together.

steps.title: A team
steps.body: As ideas take shape, teams of three to five form around the ones people want to make. Mentors, experienced volunteers who've done this before, are there to help.

steps.title: Building
steps.body: When your team hits a wall, a Mentor helps you over it, then turns it into a workshop, so the next team doesn't hit the same one.

steps.title: The Showcase
steps.body: At the end, every team shows its project in public. Anyone can use what you made, and your name stays on it.

how.shape: The busiest weeks are at the start and the end.

items.title: No lectures.
items.body: Workshops teach skills; your Pod is where you practise.

items.title: Not job placement.
items.body: You leave with something you made, with your name on it, and people who've built with you.

items.title: In person.
items.body: Evenings at your local public library, with some sessions online.

items.title: A real commitment.
items.body: Twelve weeks, busiest at the start and the end.

cycles.title: Cycle by cycle.
cycles.lede: Each cycle gets its own page: the problems, the teams, what they made and where it went. The first ones are being filled in from the Showcase.

cycle.$comment: Words for a cycle's own page.

projects.title: What the teams made
projects.empty: The projects are captured at the Showcase, with each team's consent, and go here after.

results.title: Results
results.empty: Who took part, what they made and where they went next are published after the cycle.

join.title: Twelve weeks. Something real.
join.lede: Make your free account, then apply from there when applications are open.
join.next: Then: apply, or come to a workshop first.
